title: Survey lens and modern Transformer design goals
summary: Architecture choices are treated as empirical, co-designed trade-offs among modeling quality, systems efficiency, stability, and context handling.

title: Residual stream and normalization placement
summary: Modern models move normalization out of the residual stream; prenorm preserves a clean identity path and improves gradient propagation/stability.

title: RMSNorm, bias removal, and data movement
summary: RMSNorm and bias removal are motivated largely by systems efficiency: FLOPs are not runtime when memory movement dominates.

title: Gated feed-forward activations
summary: GLU-family FFNs, especially SwiGLU/GeGLU, are common modern defaults; parameter matching motivates the 2/3 FFN-width correction.

title: Serial versus parallel Transformer blocks
summary: Parallel attention/MLP execution can improve systems utilization, but the field has largely returned to serial blocks as kernels improved and representational trade-offs mattered.

title: RoPE and relative positional structure
summary: RoPE encodes position by rotating coordinate pairs so attention inner products depend on relative offsets.

title: Consensus architecture hyperparameters
summary: FFN/model ratio, head dimensions, and depth-width aspect ratio live in broad forgiving basins with common practical defaults.

title: Vocabulary size and regularization
summary: Vocabulary size tracks multilingual/production needs; dropout is less common, while weight decay can function as an optimization aid rather than classical overfitting control.

title: Training stability: softmax, z-loss, QK norm, soft-capping
summary: Output and attention softmaxes are stability danger zones; z-loss, QK normalization, and stronger logit soft-caps address them at different costs.

title: Inference-efficient attention: KV cache, MQA, GQA
summary: Autoregressive decoding is memory-sensitive; reducing KV heads cuts cache traffic, with GQA providing a favorable efficiency/quality compromise.

title: Sliding-window and hybrid attention
summary: Alternating local/cheap layers with periodic full attention is a modern long-context cost/quality pattern; hybrid designs remain active research.
